simple: Appearance modifiers are small objects you drop inside a UI element to make it look nicer. `UIGradient` blends colors, `UIStroke` adds an outline, `UICorner` rounds the corners, `UIPadding` adds space inside the edges, and `UIShadow` adds a shadow. You do not need code for any of them; just insert one and change its properties. Mixing them turns plain boxes into polished buttons and panels.
analogy: Modifiers are like accessories for your avatar: the avatar is the same, but adding a hat, an outline glow, or a shadow makes it look totally different.
keyPoints: Each modifier works by being placed inside (as a child of) the UI object it changes.
`UIGradient` blends colors (`Color`) and see-through levels (`Transparency`) across the object; `Rotation` and `Offset` change its direction and starting point.
Gradient `Type` can be Linear, Radial, Elliptical, or Conical, and `Scale` and `TileMode` control how it repeats (these are beta features).
`UIStroke` outlines text when placed in a text object, or outlines the border of other objects; `Thickness`, `Color`, and `Transparency` style it.
`ApplyStrokeMode` set to Border puts the stroke around a text object's box instead of its letters.
`UICorner` rounds corners with `CornerRadius`: scale 0.5 or more makes a pill shape, and offset rounds by a set number of pixels.
`UIPadding` adds space between the edges of an object and its contents, such as pushing text away from a label's edges.
`UIShadow` draws a shadow behind or inside an object, with blur, color, offset, and spread settings.

terms.modifier: An object that changes how its parent looks, without being something you see on its own.
terms.gradient: A smooth blend from one color to another, like a sunset going from orange to purple.
terms.keypoint: A marker on the gradient that says "at this point, use this color". Time 0 is the start, 1 is the end.
terms.ColorSequence / NumberSequence: Lists of keypoints for colors or numbers along a gradient.
terms.stroke: An outline drawn around text or a box.
terms.Thickness: How wide the outline is, in pixels by default. 4 is thin, 12 is chunky.
terms.CornerRadius: How round the corners are. Offset 16 rounds them by 16 pixels; scale 0.5 makes a full pill shape.
terms.padding: Empty space inside the edge. A `PaddingLeft` of 10 pixels moves contents 10 pixels in from the left.
terms.blur: Soft, fuzzy edges. A bigger `BlurRadius` makes a softer shadow.
terms.spread: How much bigger or smaller the shadow is than the object.
terms.beta: A feature still being tested that you may need to turn on in Studio settings.

example.title: Make a fancy rounded button
example.place: LocalScript inside a TextButton (inside a ScreenGui in StarterGui)
example.code:
local button = script.Parent
button.BackgroundColor3 = Color3.new(1, 1, 1) -- start from a plain white button

-- Round the corners by 12 pixels
local corner = Instance.new("UICorner")
corner.CornerRadius = UDim.new(0, 12)
corner.Parent = button

-- Blue-to-purple background blend
local gradient = Instance.new("UIGradient")
gradient.Color = ColorSequence.new(Color3.fromRGB(0, 120, 255), Color3.fromRGB(150, 0, 255))
gradient.Rotation = 90 -- blend from top to bottom
gradient.Parent = button

-- Dark outline around the button's border
local stroke = Instance.new("UIStroke")
stroke.ApplyStrokeMode = Enum.ApplyStrokeMode.Border -- outline the box, not the letters
stroke.Thickness = 3
stroke.Color = Color3.fromRGB(20, 20, 40)
stroke.Parent = button

-- Keep text away from the edges
local padding = Instance.new("UIPadding")
padding.PaddingLeft = UDim.new(0, 10)
padding.PaddingRight = UDim.new(0, 10)
padding.Parent = button
explain: We start from a plain white button.
A `UICorner` rounds the corners by 12 pixels.
A `UIGradient` blends blue into purple, turned 90 degrees so it goes top to bottom.
A `UIStroke` with `ApplyStrokeMode` Border draws a dark outline around the button box instead of the text.
A `UIPadding` keeps the text 10 pixels from the left and right edges.

watchOut: A `UIStroke` inside a `TextLabel` or `TextButton` outlines the letters by default. Set `ApplyStrokeMode` to Border to outline the box.
Do not tween the `Thickness` of a stroke on text. It can cause lag or flickering.
If two strokes or shadows have the same `ZIndex`, their order is random. Give them different values.
Some gradient and shadow features are beta, so they may not work until you enable them.
